description: Erection of 1no. two storey dwellinghouse with associated landscaping, access, parking, and bin and cycle storage.
decision_conditions: The proposed development constitutes inappropriate development within the Green Belt, which is, by definition, harmful to its openness. The new dwelling would extend beyond previously developed land, and due to its height, bulk, and footprint, would have a greater impact on the openness of the Green Belt than the existing structures. No very special circumstances have been demonstrated to justify this harm. As such, the proposal is contrary to Paragraphs 142, 153, 154 and 155 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy G2 of the London Plan (2021), Policy EM2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One (2012), and Policy DMEI 4 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020).

The proposed dwelling, due to its scale, massing, and overly complex roof design, would appear visually dominant and incongruous within the setting of the locally listed 'The Hut' Public House. The suburban character and height of the dwelling would detract from the prominence and significance of the non designated heritage asset, causing less than substantial harm without any identified public benefits to justify it. The proposal fails to comply with Policies BE1, DMH 6, DMHB 3, DMHB 11, DMHB 12, and DMHB 14 of the Hillingdon Local Plan and Paragraph 135 of the NPPF (2024).

The proposed development fails to demonstrate safe and efficient vehicular access, with inadequate visibility splays, insufficient turning provision, and substandard pedestrian sightlines. The lack of clarity regarding the existing access function, combined with the potential for vehicles to reverse onto Old Orchard Close, poses a significant safety risk to road users and pedestrians. Additionally, the absence of refuse collection details prevents assessment of operational feasibility. As such, the proposal is contrary to Policies DMT 1, DMT 2 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policies T2, T4 and T6 of the London Plan (2021), and Paragraph 116 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The proposed residential development fails to demonstrate how it would mitigate potential noise and disturbance from the adjacent public house and beer garden, including an open-sided structure used for outdoor seating. In the absence of suitable mitigation measures, the proposal risks placing unreasonable restrictions on the continued operation of the existing community facility. As such, the development is contrary to Policy D13 of the London Plan (2021) and Paragraph 200 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

In the absence of a tree survey, arboricultural method statement, and root protection plan, the proposal fails to demonstrate that mature trees located along the site boundaries would be protected during construction. This lack of information prevents a full assessment of potential harm and is considered unacceptable. As such, the development is contrary to Policy DMHB 14 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020).

The proposed development fails to demonstrate compliance with Building Regulation M4(2) for accessible and adaptable dwellings. The submitted plans do not provide step-free access, a compliant entrance-level WC, or sufficient internal clearances to meet the spatial requirements of Approved Document M. As such, the proposal does not achieve the required standards of inclusive design and is contrary to Policy D7 of the London Plan (2021).

On this decision notice policies from the Councils Local Plan: Part 1 - Strategic Policies appear first, then relevant Local Plan Part 2 (2020), then London Plan Policies (2016). Hillingdon's Full Council adopted the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 1 - Strategic Policies on 8 November 2012 and the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 on 16 January 2020.

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from the  Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service.

This is a reminder that Under the terms of the Planning Act 2008 (as amended) and Community Infrastructure Levy Regulations 2010 (as amended), should an application for appeal be allowed, the proposed development would be deemed as 'chargeable development' and therefore liable to pay the London Borough of Hillingdon Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) and the Mayor of London's Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL). This would be calculated in accordance with the London Borough of Hillingdon CIL Charging Schedule 2014 and the Mayor of London's CIL Charging Schedule 2012.
For more information on CIL matters please visit the planning portal page at: www.planningportal.gov.uk/planning/applications/howtoapply/whattosubmit/cil
